purpose: Assess whether representative learners can understand, navigate and use selected ATHENA learning flows safely and accessibly.
participants: Small, deliberately varied group; include adult reviewers and age-appropriate learners only with guardian permission and child assent. Do not recruit through coercion.
minimum_safeguards: guardian informed consent where participant is a minor; child assent in age-appropriate language
no collection of sensitive health, identity, political, religious or financial details
no public posting or recording by default
participant can stop or skip without penalty
use synthetic/sample accounts and non-production data
adult safeguarding lead present and incident route defined
do not test hazardous physical activities as part of software pilot
tasks: find a module and explain the objective
complete a short learning attempt and record evidence
complete core flow in airplane mode
review and correct an adaptive suggestion
export and delete a sample record
navigate with text scaling and screen reader where relevant
measures: participant explanation of what data is collected
offline data persistence and sync status
analysis_rules: Do not treat a small convenience sample as representative population evidence.
Do not infer intelligence, diagnosis or motivation traits.
Separate observed defects from participant preference.
Record negative cases and dissent; do not report only positive quotes.
Any safeguarding event pauses the relevant activity and follows the incident pathway.
exit_criteria: No unresolved critical safety/privacy defect in tested flow.
All P0 accessibility barriers remediated or explicitly block release.
Offline writes survive restart and sync without duplicate/loss.
Participants can understand consent, sharing and delete controls.
Content owner and independent reviewers approve any revised materials.
